evidence.summary: Probe compared kernel.run(x) to kernel.reference(x) (FP64 argmax, first-index ties) with torch.equal on all rows across: 64x4096 randn; a 64x512 sweep covering every finite FP16 bit pattern (NaN/Inf excluded); all-zero and mixed rows containing +0/-0 with negatives; subnormal maxima; +/-65504 tie rows; tied maxima at multiple columns with N=257 (non-power-of-2 with masked padding lanes); N=1; contiguous storage-offset view; 128x2048 subnormal-scale values. All checks returned PASS (zero mismatched rows). Output was a fresh int64 CUDA tensor of shape [M] and x was preserved.

rationale: The packed-key reduction could mishandle signed zeros, subnormals, ties, or masked padding lanes, producing an index that differs from torch.argmax(first-index) on contract-admitted inputs.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract requires the smallest column index of the row max, positive/negative zero compare equal, all finite FP16 values including subnormals and ±65504 are legal, exact index required throughout the complete domain.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact first-maximum index for all finite FP16 inputs including signed zeros, subnormals, and ±65504; any deviation on an admitted input is a violation.
statement: The kernel returns the exact first-index stable argmax for all contract-admitted FP16 inputs (signed zeros, subnormals, ties, ±65504, various shapes/views).
